title: How we are approaching game dev with AI
author: Semantic_meaning
selftext:
A lot of disciplines need to come together to create a game. This is true at the agent level as much as it is at the human level. The agent version of this often involves jumping between different environments, tooling, models, skills, etc. It's a process that is chaotic, fatiguing, and never ending. But it does produce the best results... so we have endured this pain...until now.   
  
Workbenches is our attempt to fix that. It's an open standard that packages everything behind a certain kind of outcome: model, harness config, skills, MCP, reference files, tooling, and runtime. You might have one workbench tuned for game physics and a completely different one for art direction, and switch between them without rebuilding anything.

The video shows how I use it day to day. I plan in my own harness (Claude Code with Opus), decompose the plan to respective workbenches, they run in the cloud in parallel (close my laptop), and each one comes back on its own branch. I do a light amount of work with CC to assemble them, and it goes up as one PR.

You can also pull down other people's workbenches. A few game ones are up now (three.js, Godot), and the goal is that the developers and artists you admire can publish how they get their results, so your game can end up using a blend of their workbenches and your own.  
  
Happy to throw some tokens your way for you to kick the tires, and if you've built games with AI and have a method you think gets better results than everyone else's, I want to talk. We're setting up paid workbenches where creators earn from every run.

comments.author: Semantic_meaning
comments.body: Link to check it out (again let me know you came from here and I'll get you started) : [https://workbenches.dev](https://workbenches.dev)

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: I always avoid 3rd party workflows like this as the plague! I always say if people are not able to build their own workflows like this they should just avoid AI all together! 🧠

replies.author: Semantic_meaning
replies.body: you can build your own workflows as workbenches easily. this just gives you the ability to 'dockerize' the configs behind those workflows

comments.author: StrongLegStrongMan
comments.body:
What have you made? How grand is your project. Everyone is trying to tell everyone how to work with AI yet no great game has been released yet. My group of people are undertaking a massive project, making the singularity of video games. Someone from my group is who I am looking for to call Senpai. 

Total War, Sims, City Skylines, Zoo Tycoon, Skyrim - put them all together and make an Epic game.

Write a book on top of it all!

replies.author: Semantic_meaning
replies.body:
Totally fair challenge. We haven't shipped something Skyrim level. But Workbenches isn't us telling anyone how to build their game. It's a place for engineers, designers, and artists who are better at this than we are to store how they get their results, so other people can build on it inside the workflow they already prefer.   
  
Here's a small benchmark as an example : [https://workbenches.dev/benchmarks/espresso-liquid](https://workbenches.dev/benchmarks/espresso-liquid)
